description: WHAT WAS PROMISED TO A CUSTOMER, WHAT IT IS WORTH, AND WHEN EACH PART OF IT IS EARNED. The ASC 606 unit of account, which a Sales Order cannot carry: the distinct performance obligations, the transaction price allocated between them, whether control transfers at a point in time or over time, and the schedule that turns all of that into journal entries. On a produce operation the gap this closes is at its widest — fruit delivered in September against a settlement that arrives in December at a price nobody knew in September.

fields.description: What this contract is called in conversation — 'Stemilt 2026 Gala pool', 'CA storage agreement 2026'. The docname is built from it and the company abbreviation.
fields.label: Contract Name

fields.description: Whose contract this is. A REQUIRED Link to Company, so Frappe's own User Permission scoping restricts it with no hook of this app's own.
fields.label: Company

fields.description: The counterparty. Required: ASC 606 is about contracts WITH CUSTOMERS, and an arrangement with no customer on it is something else.
fields.label: Customer

fields.description: Where the contract has got to. `Completed` means every obligation is satisfied and every scheduled tranche recognised; it is set by whoever decides that, not computed, because a contract can be finished commercially with a tail of recognition still to run.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: ASC 606-10-25-27. OVER TIME where the customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefit — controlled-atmosphere storage, a management agreement. POINT IN TIME where control transfers on a day — a bin of fruit changing hands. It is a property of the contract for reporting; each schedule row still carries its own basis, because a contract can genuinely contain both.
fields.label: Recognition

fields.description: What the operation expects to be entitled to for the whole contract. On a consignment pool this is an ESTIMATE until the settlement arrives, which is exactly what ASC 606's variable-consideration guidance is about — update it with update_revenue_contract as the estimate firms, and the schedule and the obligation sums are re-checked against the new figure.
fields.label: Transaction Price

fields.description: Computed on save: the schedule's total. Stored because a list view cannot aggregate a child table, and 'which contracts have an incomplete schedule' is the question somebody scans this list to answer.
fields.label: Scheduled

fields.description: Credited when a tranche is recognised. Left blank, recognize_revenue_milestone refuses rather than guessing — an account picked by an algorithm is a misstatement somebody finds at year end.
fields.label: Revenue Account

fields.description: Debited when a tranche is recognised — contract asset or receivable. Also never guessed.
fields.label: Receivable Account

fields.description: The distinct promises. One is the common case and is not a failure to decompose — a contract to deliver one lot of fruit contains one promise.
fields.label: Obligations

fields.description: When each part is earned. Milestone rows wait for their obligation; time rows come due on their date.
fields.label: Schedule

name: Revenue Contract
